name: Geneva Graduate Institute (IHEID) Master Scholarships (Full/Partial Scholarship + Tuition Reduction)
requiredDocuments: Completed online application form (also serves as the financial-aid application — fill in the financial-situation fields)
Transcripts and degree certificates/diplomas covering all university-level courses attempted (official electronic copies at application; originals required at enrolment if admitted)
Contact details for 2-3 academic (or professional) referees, entered in the application form (they are contacted automatically)
Motivation letter explaining why you choose the programme and the Institute

English proficiency certificate at CEFR C1 (IELTS Academic 7.0 overall / TOEFL iBT 100+ / Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 185+) — may be submitted conditionally with a booked test appointment (certificate due by 30 May 2026)
Certified translations of any documents not in English, Spanish, French, German or Italian
For financial aid: proof of income, tax statements, bank statements and other documents evidencing all income, liquidities, capital and potential family/organisation contributions
Application fee payment (CHF 100 for the 15 January deadline)

timeline.deadline: 15 January 2026 (the only round in which master applicants can request financial aid; closes midnight Geneva time CET)
timeline.notes: Anchored to 2026-06: this documents the September 2026 intake, whose application/financial-aid window opened 1 October 2025 and whose master financial-aid deadline (15 January 2026) has already passed. The Institute states its NEXT intake is September 2027, with applications opening in October 2026; the master financial-aid deadline is expected to remain 15 January (i.e. ~15 January 2027) but exact 2026-2027 dates were not yet published at access time. Master financial aid can ONLY be requested in the January round.

benefits: Full or partial scholarship of maximum CHF 20,000 per year for two years (cost-of-living stipend disbursed in monthly instalments)
Tuition reduction (applied directly to the student account); standard master tuition is CHF 8,000/year for non-residents, CHF 5,000/year for Swiss residents

A full award = stipend + tuition coverage (fully funded); a partial award may be stipend only, tuition reduction only, or a combination, set by the Financial Aid Committee on need + merit within available funds
Need-blind admission: financial circumstances are not seen by the admission committee
Renewable for a second year if financial need continues (re-apply in April-May, demonstrating continued need and academic progress)
Free compulsory French courses (3-week intensive + weekly first-year course) for students below B1
Awards designed to cover the full study programme: 4 semesters for a master's degree

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: The Institute does not publish an admission/selection rate for the scholarship. It does state that 'Each year, 10-15% of admitted Master's students receive full or partial scholarships' (https://www.graduateinstitute.ch/application) — this is a funding-award share among admitted students, NOT an acceptance/selection rate.

mustKnow: Master financial aid can ONLY be requested at the 15 January deadline, in the same form as the admission application — if you miss the January round you cannot apply for aid later, ever.

'Fully funded' is not automatic: only 10-15% of admitted master's students receive any full OR partial scholarship, and a partial award may be just a tuition reduction with no living stipend. Aid is need + merit based and limited by available funds.
Stipend recipients MUST reside in Switzerland or neighbouring France during studies and presence is periodically checked (post-enrolment condition, not an entry bar).
The living-cost stipend is reduced if the student's total income exceeds CHF 32,000 in the academic year.

No nationality restriction and admission is need-blind; the Institute supports students 'regardless of origin' and a Bangladeshi master's student is a documented scholarship recipient, so a Bangladeshi national is eligible.
Application fee is CHF 100 for the 15 January deadline and CANNOT be waived (only postponed for applicants whose country's banking system is under international sanctions).
No minimum GPA is set ('We do not set minimum grade point average requirements'); files are judged comparatively across 100+ education systems.
English proficiency is required at CEFR C1 (IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 100), waived only if you completed at least one year of full-time university study taught entirely in English.
PhD funding works completely differently (automatic 4-year package); this record covers the MASTER's-level need-and-merit aid only.

universities: Geneva Graduate Institute (Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies, IHEID)

eligibleNationalities: Open to applicants from around the world with no nationality restriction; admission is need-blind and the Institute supports talented students 'regardless of origin'. About 85% of students are international. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible (a Bangladeshi master's student is a documented scholarship recipient).
languageRequirements: English at CEFR C1 — IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (6.5 minimum subscores), TOEFL iBT 100+, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency (185+ total, 180+ subscores). May be submitted conditionally with a booked test appointment (certificate due by 30 May 2026). Waived for native English speakers and those who completed at least one year of full-time university study taught entirely in English. French is NOT required for admission.
standardizedTests: Not required for master's programmes (GRE is required only for the PhD in International Economics).
minGPA: No minimum GPA — the Institute explicitly does not set a grade-point requirement.
applicationFee: CHF 100 for the 15 January deadline (cannot be waived; may be postponed only for applicants whose country's banking system is under international sanctions).
fundingCovers: Living-cost stipend (maximum CHF 20,000/year, disbursed in monthly instalments)
monthlyStipend: Full scholarship is a maximum of CHF 20,000 per year, disbursed in monthly instalments (the exact master monthly amount/schedule is not published; the comparable PhD package disburses CHF 2,000/month over September-June). Partial awards are lower or tuition-only.
renewalConditions: Renewable for a second year if financial need remains; master students must submit a new renewal application in April-May and demonstrate continued financial need and academic progress.
postStudyWork: Swiss regulations permit foreign students to work part-time (15 hours/week) during term and full-time during vacations; non-EU students may not work during their first six months. The Institute does not itself grant a post-study work right.
